messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT: KV_CACHE_PRESSURE on inference-prod. alerts: kv-cache-eviction-high, slab_fragments_up. p95 baseline 120ms -> current ~840ms, p99 spike to ~3.2s. streaming stalls observed (partial responses / stalls at tail). trigger: sustained prefill rate surge on shard-pool s-32. creating thread for triage.
jen: seeing the same on grafana — kv.slab.fragments spiked ~5x, prefill > decode by ~3x on a few nodes. streaming tail latency jumps line up with high eviction count. taking first pass.
mike: joining, what’s the customer impact? errors or just slowness?
customer-ops: got 2 customers reporting chat responses >5s and some websocket disconnects. tagging affected tenants: corp-x, partner-y.
jen: quick check: p95 across routes: gen-route 750ms, streaming-route 1.2s (p95). p99 across routes: gen-route 2.8s, streaming-route 5.4s. trace samples show prefill io waits and decode queue backlog.
sre_lead: good context. likely fragmentation + eviction storms causing heavier decode stalls for streamed sessions. mitigation options: 1) throttle prefill concurrency for non-streaming routes, 2) bump eviction aggressiveness for low-priority slabs, 3) route streaming traffic away from s-32 pool to reduce tail. prefer non-disruptive first: throttle prefill and adjust eviction config.
jen: agreed. applying prefill throttle patch to config service for pool s-32. will also add a temporary route tag to avoid prefill on streaming sessions.
jen: command I’m running (CI config patch):
```
curl -X PATCH https://config.internal/api/v1/pools/s-32 -H 'Authorization: Bearer $CI_TOKEN' -d '{"prefill": {"max_concurrency": 6, "enable_for_streaming": false}}'
```
mike: FYI logs from node s-32-04 show many `decode_queue_wait_ms` > 2000ms:``
2026-04-12T08:10:02Z s-32-04 decode_queue_wait_ms=2140 tenant=corp-x request_id=abc123
2026-04-12T08:10:03Z s-32-04 eviction_triggered=true slab_id=7 freed=128kb
```
jen: patch applied. watching grafana now.
jen: 5m after change: p95 down to ~300ms, p99 ~1.1s overall. streaming p95 still at ~900ms with occasional stalls. partial improvement.
sre_lead: good progress. next step: temporarily re-route streaming traffic off s-32 to s-16 and s-20 pools to isolate. @infra-eng can we shift routing policy for streaming traffic for the next 30m?
infra-eng: can do. applying route map change now, will gradually shift via traffic policy (weight 0.7 -> s-16,s-20).
infra-eng: route change applied. monitoring.
jen: after routing shift streaming p95 dropped to ~320ms, p99 to ~1.5s, stalls reduced but not eliminated. looks like eviction pressure propagated across pool earlier; still need longer-term fix.
mike: noticed increased slab fragmentation metric persists; suspect prefill vs decode imbalance — prefill filling many small slabs while decode holds large KV pages. suggests we need a defrag job or change allocation policy.
sre_lead: agree. inc bot, please open incident and assign severity. we should also notify affected customers briefly.
incident-bot: Created INC-2026-512 (Severity: S3). Pager duties: @sre_lead assigned. Postmortem owner: jen.
customer-ops: sending a short status update to corp-x and partner-y: "We are mitigating increased latency on inference endpoints; partial recovery in progress. Expect improvements in next 30–45 minutes. We’ll follow up with RCA." :thumbsup:
jen: rolling log sample and a quick diagnostic I ran that shows decode stall stack for affected worker: ```
stack: runtime_handle->kv_prefill_worker->decode_worker->await_io (blocked 1.8s)
metrics: prefill_ops=420/s decode_ops=130/s
```
sre_lead: for next actions: 1) schedule slab defrag job in low-traffic window (overnight), 2) adjust allocator heuristics to prefer larger allocations for decode hot keys, 3) implement prefill backpressure when decode queue depth > threshold, 4) long-term: work on shard-level routing to prevent cross-eviction blast. assign owners: (1) infra-eng, (2) eng-runtime, (3) jen (quick patch), (4) platform-arch.
jen: I’ll open follow-up tickets and push the quick prefill backpressure patch (small change).
sre_lead: ok — handoff to me for the rest of the on-call. summary for next shift: partial mitigation applied (prefill throttle + routing), observable improvement (p95/p99 down significantly), streaming isolated to different pools, persistent slab fragmentation and need defrag + allocator changes. customer impact: increased latency with a few websocket disconnect reports, no broad error rate spike. timeline and actions in the incident ticket.
jen: handing off. key runbook actions left: monitor p99, watch streaming stalls, finish prefill backpressure PR, coordinate defrag timeframe with infra.
sre_lead: ack — taking lead. jen, mike, infra-eng — thanks for quick response. will follow up with post-incident review.
jen: thanks — leaving notes in the incident for postmortem.
customer-ops: will update customers with latest ETA and close the loop after RCA.
incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-512 updated: status=mitigated, impact=latency elevated, next_update=+45m.
